source_text: The terminological divergence underscores perceptual gaps: while international bodies and Indian activists invoke "mutilation" to evoke harm and advocate prohibition, community narratives prioritize cultural continuity, with khatna invoked in intra-community discourse as an innocuous rite of passage, not a violation warranting the pejorative "FGM" label that homogenizes disparate practices. [19]
